items.title: Agencies launch centralized platform for managing independent dispute resolution operations - American Hospital Association
items.reason: This item directly addresses operational implementation of the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, a core component of No Surprises Act enforcement that revenue-cycle teams depend on.
items.summary: Federal agencies have launched a centralized platform for managing Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) operations under the No Surprises Act. This platform consolidates IDR administration, which handles disputes over out-of-network balance bills and other surprise billing claims. The centralized system affects hospitals, insurers, and dispute resolution entities involved in the IDR process. Revenue-cycle teams will need to adapt workflows and systems to interact with this new platform for submitting, tracking, and resolving IDR claims.

items.title: UnitedHealth sues CMS over 2027 Medicare Advantage ratings - Minnesota Lawyer
items.reason: This reports a lawsuit by a major payer (UnitedHealth) against CMS, a direct fit for payer litigation and enforcement topics that affect revenue cycle through Medicare Advantage reimbursement and rating mechanisms.
items.summary: UnitedHealth Group has filed a lawsuit against the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) challenging the agency's 2027 Medicare Advantage ratings methodology. The suit contests CMS's rating framework that affects plan star ratings and bonuses for Medicare Advantage insurers, which directly influences payment adjustments and financial performance under the MA program. Revenue-cycle teams are affected because MA ratings determine plan competitiveness, enrollment projections, and capitated reimbursement levels that drive provider payments and network stability for the upcoming plan year. This litigation outcome could reshape how CMS calculates ratings, impacting provider contract negotiations and payment forecasts tied to plan performance metrics.

items.title: CMS proposes $107B Medicare Advantage Star Ratings pay cut - Modern Healthcare News
items.reason: CMS enforcement action proposing substantial Medicare Advantage payment reductions based on Star Ratings performance directly impacts payer revenues and represents regulatory action by CMS against MA plans, which is core to payer litigation and enforcement.
items.summary: CMS has proposed a $107 billion reduction in Medicare Advantage payments based on Star Ratings performance metrics. This regulatory action by CMS targets Medicare Advantage plans' reimbursement levels, with payment adjustments tied to quality-of-care ratings. The proposal affects all Medicare Advantage insurers and their financial performance. For revenue-cycle teams, this represents a major regulatory enforcement mechanism that will significantly impact MA plan revenues and require operational adjustments to quality metrics and billing practices to mitigate payment reductions.
